requirement.description: Risk assessment for new data sources is still done by hand. That is simply how new data sources get reviewed today.
requirement.fact: Risk assessment for new data sources is still done by hand.
requirement.reading: That is simply how new data sources get reviewed today.

narrator.name: Requirements Reuben
narrator.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

inputs.hint: The fact is that something does not exist. Describe only how the work is done today without it, as observed events or numbers. No consequences, risks, costs or benefits.

output.content: I pulled the intake logs for the last six months of new data source requests. Each entry shows the same pattern. A requester submits a form, and a team member opens it manually. They check the source against the privacy policy, verify the retention limits, and confirm the access controls. There is no automated flag or system alert. The reviewer writes their notes directly into the ticket. The average time from submission to a completed review is four days. I saw no instances where a tool pre validated the metadata before a human looked at it. The individual checks each field by hand before the ticket moves to the next stage.
output.reclassify_reason: The text describes the observed workflow and metrics (such as the four-day average review time and lack of automation) without expressing any wishes, refusals, or stated trade-offs.
